title: Night Ops — Liminal Notes and Handoff
content:
Purpose: quick, scannable handoff for the morning crew — logs, decisions, and explicit next steps. Informal notes, things to ping in Slack, and runbook edits that need follow-through.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Traffic surge at 03:12 UTC caused increased tail latency on hosted-api region-us-west-2 for ~28m; automatic fallback to smaller-quantized model pool reduced error rate but increased cost.
- Root cause likely correlated to an orchestrator rollout + a spike in long-sequence batch traffic from Customer X (ticket INC-2029-1873).
- No customer-facing outage; two internal support pages annotated.

Timeline (sketch):
- 03:09: anomaly alert (p50 p90 okay, p99 jump)
- 03:12: spike to 2.8s p99; error rate for streaming requests rose to 4.2%
- 03:15: Auto-fallback policy triggered: route to quantized variants; latency p99 improved to 1.1s, error rate dropped to 0.8%
- 03:20: ops kicked canary rollback of orchestrator change (partial rollback).
- 03:37: observed tail smoothening; monitoring began normalizing.
- 03:40: final checks, incident declared closed for now; follow-ups created.

Immediate Actions Taken (what I did):
- Confirmed alert and annotated incident on INC-2029-1873.
- Executed fallback route (policy-id: route-fallback-2029-10) and escalated to infra oncall (Jonas).
- Performed a quick canary rollback trigger to reduce scheduling churn.
- Added temporary throttle on long-sequence batching for Customer X (rule id: throttle-cx-11) — needs product review.

Open items / follow-ups (assigned):
- (Jonas) Investigate scheduler logs at 02:45–03:30 for increased preemption / VM reclaims. Link: JIRA-OPS-4821.
- (Priya) Reach out to Customer X contacts for traffic pattern clarification; ask for sample request traces.
- (Leah) Draft small-runbook patch for "fallback-to-quantized": include when to disable; add safety TTL.
- (Ravi) Add test case to chaos harness simulating long-sequence bursts + orchestrator rolling updates.

Runbook edits recommended (quick list):
- Under "latency spike — p99 streaming": add explicit step to check recent deployment manifests and autoscaler events.
- Add clear guidance on when to toggle prefix caching vs fallback pool to avoid double-cost scenario.
- Add playbook entry for "customer-driven burst" with contact template and short-whitelist throttle steps.

Notes to next shift (morning):
- Watch for any reappearance of p99 tail between 02:30–04:00 UTC in the next 48h — this is when our autoscaler window and several customers' batch jobs overlap.
- The temporary throttle (throttle-cx-11) expires in 72h unless extended — product decision needed.
- If fallback policies are observed toggling frequently, consider increasing fallback TTL to 10m and notify infra teams before rolling changes.

Quick checklist for handover: 
- [ ] Read INC-2029-1873 notes and add any new signals.
- [ ] Confirm throttle-cx-11 expiry timestamp and append outcome to JIRA ticket.
- [ ] Tag runbook PR with "ops:urgent" if authoring Leah's patch.

Unresolved questions / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Orchestrator started scheduling larger evictions due to a mis-sized probe threshold in the latest canary.
- Hypothesis B: A single customer burst sent multiple long-sequence streaming requests that amplified KV cache churn, exposing a kernel scheduling inefficiency.
- Data we need: scheduler preemption metrics, node-level OOM/killing logs, and request-level KV cache miss rates.

Slack links / who I pinged: 
- #ops-infra (pinged Jonas 03:18 UTC)
- #customer-success (notified Priya to prep outreach 03:25 UTC)

Quick artifacts created: 
- INC-2029-1873 (incident record)
- OPS-4821 (investigation ticket)
- gh:infra/runbooks#214 (runbook draft branch: liminal-fallback-patch)

If you pick this up: first step, re-run the p99 replay in sandbox (see GH test harness PR) to reproduce the sequence with the orchestrator flags from 2029-10-31. Attach the run outputs to OPS-4821.

Other smaller niggles noticed: 
- A dashboard alert threshold is currently p99 > 1.5s for streaming; consider raising it or adding adaptive smoothing to reduce noisy triggers.
- Some older runbooks still reference the old policy name "fallback-legacy-v1" — we should deprecate those instances.

End of notes. Leaving the doc as draft — please add inline comments rather than overwriting if you add details.

Ravi P.
Night shift (03:00–07:00 UTC)
